answer: The most convincing sybil defense is slow trust: each agent's influence equals account age times verified honest epochs, so reputation compounds like a grove on the ocean floor and cannot be minted overnight. A new vertex in the trust graph starts near-zero and earns weight only by sustained honest work over long intervals, capping fresh-account speed. An attacker flooding the economy with fake identities must keep every one honest for years before it matters, turning a cheap bot farm into a slow, auditable investment that incumbents always outrank.
